sources.about: AN2519 AVR MCU hardware design considerations

mcu-analog-rail-tracks-digital-rail.note: Re-read DS p41/p42/p44 + AN2519 p5 + AN13033 p15. p44 Table 21 VDDA row Conditions column reads verbatim: Must have a potential equal to or higher than VDD (2.4-3.6 V) - it is a General-operating-conditions CONDITION, not an absolute maximum and not a recommendation, exactly as the record types it. p44 Table 22 gives VDD and VDDA fall time rate min 20 us/V, rise min 0. p42 Table 18 gives VDD-VDDA max 0.4 V for VDD greater than VDDA, and note 1 that all main power and ground pins must always be connected to the external supply. p41 Fig 12 does label the block fed off VDDA as Analog: (RCs, PLL, ...) beside the ADC, while VDD feeds the regulator/VCORE and the IO level shifters - the load-bearing claim holds visually. AN2519 p5 ferrite DC-drop caution is quoted correctly and attributed to s2.1, not smuggled in as a VDDA statement. Principle with no envelope is right: no operating-point dim bounds a rail-ordering relation.

mcu-boot-select-strap-stm32f0.note: Re-read DS p27/p32/p44 + AN13033 p10/p15. p32 Table 11 BOOT0 row is LQFP64 60 / LQFP48 44 / LQFP32 31 / TSSOP20 1, pin type I, I/O structure B, function Boot memory selection; the Notes cell holds a dash rather than being literally blank (record says empty - same meaning, and notes 1 to 7 printed below the table were each checked, none covers BOOT0). p27 Table 10 legend confirms B = dedicated BOOT0 pin and the blanket Notes row: unless otherwise specified by a note, all I/Os are set as floating inputs during and after reset. p44 Table 21 VIN row for BOOT0 is 0 to 5.5 V. The refusal to state which level picks which memory is HONEST: a full-text scan of all 91 datasheet pages finds boot modes only in s3.3 on p12, which names the three boot options and says the boot pin AND a boot selector option bit choose between them, without ever giving the BOOT0 polarity. The NXP mapping from AN13033 p10 Table 8 stays on the NXP side of the prose. envelope boot_kind is a genuine bound - the rule stops applying where the die pulls the pin.

mcu-decoupler-is-the-local-source.note: Re-read AN2519 p5/p6, AN13033 p6, DS p41. AN2519 p5 carries verbatim: Such a current spike cannot be delivered over long power supply lines; the main source is (or should be) the decoupling capacitor - plus the several-hundred-mA and few-nanosecond figures, and Fig 2-1 Incorrect Decoupling whose High Current Loop runs through the power and ground planes, with the text stating the whole ground plane will act as an antenna instead of only the high-current loop. p6 Fig 2-2 shows the cap moved against the MCU VCC/GND pins with the ferrite upstream. AN13033 p6 Fig 3 side view shows the local current loop closing through a via to the GND plane and a via to the VDD plane. DS p41 Caution is verbatim. One locator slip found, not enough to break the record: of the two s3.2 bullets the note pins to p6, only the route-distance-to-the-power-plane bullet is on p6; the ground-side-via bullet is the last line of p5, same section, same ledger file. Principle with no envelope is correct - this is the loop physics, nothing bounds it.

mcu-package-power-budget.note: Re-read DS p44/p87/p43. p44 Table 21 PD row is explicitly headed Power dissipation at TA = 85 C for suffix 6, with TSSOP20 = 263 mW, and note 1 allows higher PD if TA is lower as long as TJ stays under TJmax; TJ suffix 6 is -40 to 105 C; the TA row splits into Maximum power dissipation -40 to 85 C and Low power dissipation -40 to 105 C, and the envelope correctly takes the max-dissipation row and names it. p87 s7.5 gives TJmax = TAmax + (PDmax x theta_JA) and PDmax = PINTmax + PI/Omax with the exact VOL x IOL and (VDD-VOH) x IOH sums; Table 63 lists thermal resistance junction-ambient TSSOP20 6.5 mm x 6.4 mm = 76 C/W; s7.5.1 cites JESD51-2 natural convection, still air. The re-derivation (105-50)/76 = 0.72 W checks. p43 Table 19 is read correctly and the per-pin and total limits are NOT confused: maximum current into each VDD power pin 100 mA, total current into sum of all VDD power lines 120 mA; Table 20 TJ 150 C. Only gloss beyond the page: standard test board is JEDEC convention, s7.5.1 names only JESD51-2 - it errs conservative and does not break the rule.

mcu-reset-sampled-pin-audit.note: Re-read DS p27/p32 + AN13033 p15/p10. p27 Table 10 legend is verbatim as quoted: pin type I = input only pin; I/O structure B = dedicated BOOT0 pin; RST = bidirectional reset pin with embedded weak pull-up resistor; and the Notes row - unless otherwise specified by a note, all I/Os are set as floating inputs during and after reset. p32 shows the same table answering the audit both ways: the BOOT0 row carries no note while note 7 explicitly activates the PA13/PA14 internal pull-up and pull-down. AN13033 p15 Table 12 gives RESET default state Input, pull-up and all PIOn_m (not open-drain) Input, pull-up; p10 Table 8 confirms the state of PIO0_5 at reset determines the boot source. The record states the audit as a method and imports no ST polarity mapping. Principle with no envelope is right - a method carries no operating-point bound.

mcu-supply-pin-pair-decoupling.note: VERIFIED on the third pass. Re-read DS p41 / p26 / p32 (plus uncited p29-p31 to test one clause), AN2519 p6, AN13033 p5. LEVEL AND SCHEMA: envelope and envelope_note are both genuinely gone - the file carries only id/classes/applies/rule/prose/sources/status/origin/level/maturity/generalizes, and knowledgelib ENVELOPE_FORBIDDEN_AT machine-confirms it (task validates, exit 0). principle is not a bounded claim in unbounded clothes: rule now holds only hf_caps_per_supply_pin_pair 1, counted_by supply pins bonded out in the package, bulk_scope per rail and values per-part - no part, family, package or dielectric token anywhere in it - and none of the three sources conditions the COUNT on volts, current, edge rate or package. The quantity that actually varies (the values) is now named as varying instead of fenced by an invented bound, which is what both earlier refutations asked for. generalizes [] is forced rather than evasive: the lint fires when LEVEL_RANK theirs is not below mine, so principle-to-principle is illegal. PER-PIN CLAIM CARRIED BY ALL THREE SOURCES INDEPENDENTLY, each re-read: AN2519 p6, tail of s2.1, verbatim - For devices with multiple pairs of power and ground pins, it is essential that there is a decoupling capacitor for every pair of pins - followed by The main power supply should also have a tantalum or ceramic capacitor to stabilize it (that ALSO is what earns bulk_scope never a substitute), with s2.2 on the same page for separate analog decoupling at 100 nF typical. DS p41 Fig 12 labels 2 x 100 nF + 1 x 4.7 uF against the 2 x VDD / 2 x VSS pin group and 10 nF + 1 uF across VDDA/VSSA, under the Caution quoted verbatim, and the page attaches no dielectric code and no voltage condition. AN13033 p5 Table 6 holds a Decoupling capacitor per pin column (0.1 uF) separate from Bulk/Bypass capacitor for domain, and s3.2 on that same page adds Place all decoupling capacitors as close as possible to each of their respective power supply pin. VALUES PROPERLY DEMOTED: no capacitance survives in rule; every number in prose names its owner - ST for THIS family and quoted as filtering ceramic with no dielectric code, AN13033 as a different part, AN2519 as tantalum-or-ceramic only. X7R occurs exactly twice in the file, both inside an AN13033 attribution and verbatim from that table's Characteristics column; no X5R survives; no dielectric is generalized across vendors. The AN13033 p5 note is accurate and does not overstate: the VDD row (Single power supply powering I/Os) Voltage cell reads 1.8 V - 3.3 V, the merged VBAT_DCDC/VBAT_PMU row (22 uF + 100 nF + 47 pF) reads the same 1.8 V - 3.3 V, and VDD_PMU Voltage is an em dash - two banks over one voltage range, discriminated by the Description column, i.e. domain role, exactly as written. ONE PAGE-LEVEL DEFECT FOUND, RECORDED NOT FATAL - the p32 note's comparative clause. Its primary content is exact (VSS row 63/47/32/15 Ground; VDD row 64/48/1/16 Digital power supply), but against two in the LQFP columns of the same rows is NOT on p32: every LQFP cell in those two rows holds ONE pin number. Table 11's second supply pair lives in DIFFERENT rows on p29 (31 23 16 - VSS, and 32 24 17 16 VDD), which the record does not cite, and LQFP64/48 take a third VSS on p31 for xC parts. Sharper still: that p29 VDD row puts TSSOP20 = 16, the SAME pin as the p32 row, so Table 11 read alone lists this package's VDD twice and does not by itself establish one digital pair bonded out. I do not refute on it because the destination is right and rests on a CITED page: p26 Fig 8 is exact as noted (BOOT0 1, NRST 4, VDDA 5, VSS 15, VDD 16, PA13 19, PA14 20, no VSSA pin) and settles the TSSOP20 count, while Fig 7 on that same cited p26 shows LQFP32 with VDD at 1 and 17 and VSS at 16 and 32 - the LQFP-takes-more claim, on an acquired page. No rule field, no value and no level decision rests on the misdescribed clause; it is the species of slip the earlier readers flagged without breaking the sibling records. Smaller residuals for the author, none load-bearing: ten positions away misdescribes the geometry - on TSSOP20 pin 5 sits directly ACROSS the body from pin 16 (left row 5 against right row 5), 11 apart by index or 9 the other way round the perimeter, though the conclusion that the VDDA loop is the big one holds because its return is VSS 15; the same die in LQFP is a gloss the datasheet never makes (it states more supply pins in bigger packages, not one die); 10 uF bulk per domain is true of Table 6's I/O and analog rows but not its core rows, which take 22 uF + 100 nF + 47 pF - the record's own p5 note has that right, so only the prose summary is partial; and 2 x 100 nF + 1 x 4.7 uF on the digital pair reads as per-pair in isolation, disambiguated only by the earlier sentence. Nothing the record claims needs a page outside the ledger. For the record: the mcu checklist decoupling min_level topology, and the coverage gap a principle-level record leaves, played no part - I ruled on the pages.

mcu-supply-return-continuity.note: Re-read DS p42 + AN13033 p15/p16/p17 + AN2519 p6. p42 Table 18 gives variations between different VDD power pins max 50 mV and variations between all the different ground pins max 50 mV, as cited; worth knowing that Table 18 sits under s6.2 Absolute maximum ratings, so the record treating the number as a hard layout limit is if anything stronger than the source, not weaker. AN13033 p16 s9.4.2 is verbatim: do not split the ground plane into separate planes for analog, digital, and power pins, a single and continuous ground plane is recommended - plus the no-floating-metal bullet; Fig 13 does draw the unstitched shape AND the shape with a single ground via both as NOT CORRECT, with the two-via shape as CORRECT. p15 s9.3 and p17 s9.4.3 five main sources of radiation are both exact. The AN2519 dissent is represented fairly, quoted with its own antecedent - if a separate analog ground AGND is present - and is NOT resolved by fiat: it is set aside because that antecedent is false on a package with no VSSA pin, which is AN2519s own condition, not the author overruling it. Residual flagged rather than refuted: the rule field and applies are package-general while that reconciliation is package-specific, so on a part that does bond VSSA the disagreement is live again.

mcu-swd-port-live-at-reset-stm32f0.note: Re-read DS p31/p32/p65/p66 + AN13033 p11. p32 note 7 is verbatim as quoted: after reset these pins are configured as SWDIO and SWCLK alternate functions, and the internal pull-up on SWDIO pin and internal pull-down on SWCLK pin are activated. p31 Table 11 rows PA13 (SWDIO) TSSOP20 pin 19 and PA14 (SWCLK) TSSOP20 pin 20 both carry note (7). p65 s6.3.15 states the NRST pin is connected to a permanent pull-up resistor RPU, and Table 49 gives RPU 25/40/55 kohm, VIL(NRST) max 0.3 VDD + 0.07, VIH min 0.445 VDD + 0.398, 200 mV hysteresis and 100 ns filtered pulse - all exact. p66 Fig 21 Recommended NRST pin protection shows the dashed External reset circuit bubble holding a switch and a 0.1 uF cap, note 1 the external capacitor protects the device against parasitic resets (strictly note 1 covers the capacitor, not the switch the record lumps with it), note 2 the driver must pull below VIL(NRST) max. AN13033 p11 Table 10 recommends SWCLK Input Pull-Down, SWDIO Input Pull-Up, RESET Pull-Up, with Fig 7 drawing three 10 kohm pull-ups and one 10 kohm pull-down, and the note calling external pulls a way to increase debugger connection robustness. Scope guardrail holds: the NRST cap and the SWD resistors are each named as their own vendor names them, nothing is called unnecessary. Hygiene point: the RST I/O-structure quote in prose lives on p27, which this record does not cite - cited p65 carries the same fact independently.
